title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows and optimize cache + parallelism
author: Diego Morales
description: Splits the monolithic CI workflow into focused lint, test and release workflows and introduces cache/key hygiene and parallelism improvements to reduce walltime and increase cache hit rates. Motivation: current combined workflow has grown unwieldy and causes long queue times and frequent cache misses; splitting allows targeted runs, faster feedback, and smaller CI artifacts. This PR: 1) introduces .github/workflows/lint.yml, test.yml and release.yml derived from the old ci.yml; 2) consolidates and standardizes cache keys across JS/Python/Go builds; 3) parallelizes test matrix where safe (unit/test-integration separation) and adds guarded concurrency for heavier integration tests; 4) extracts common pipeline scripts into infra/ci/scripts/ and a small cache helper infra/ci/cache.sh; 5) updates release automation to use a lightweight prepare step and separate publish job to avoid long-running combined job timeouts; 6) updates several repo-level Makefile targets and README CI docs. Rollout plan: merge to main, monitor CI queue length and cache hit metrics during next 48 hours, revert gate on release workflow if any regressions. Note: this is a refactor-only change with no runtime behavior changes to services. Checklist: [x] new workflow files added [x] cache keys tested locally [x] unit+lint workflow run green on head branch [x] canary release job dry-run successful on release branch. Related: ENG-6123 (ci perf), ENG-6130 (release automation hygiene).

review_comments: Priya Kaur: Nice cleanup. A few questions: can we keep the old ci.yml around for 1 week as a fallback? Also please add a short note about cache key versioning so team members know when to bump keys.

Diego Morales: Agree on the fallback; I've kept a trimmed copy at .github/workflows/ci.legacy.yml for one week and added comments in infra/ci/cache.sh about key versioning and when to bump (CACHE_V=1).

Luca Bianchi: Parallel test runner looks good, but I noted flaky tests X and Y when run in parallel; added suggestions to tools/ci/parallel-test-runner.py to force-sequential for those tests. Please add an env guard to skip parallelization on PRs with label 'no-parallel'.
Diego Morales: Added a PR label check and the NO_PARALLEL env guard; updated docs. I also added an integration test gate to ensure heavy tests run only on schedule or on release branches.
Maya Chen: CI matrix increase may raise runner usage costs; can we add an autoscale cap or concurrency limit for non-critical jobs?
Diego Morales: Added concurrency:ci and a short note in README. We'll monitor runner usage and revert if cost impact is material.
ci_summary: Initial run: lint and unit matrix green; integration job failed (flaky tests) on first run; fixes applied and rerun; final: all checks passed. Cargo/Golang lint check updated to new action and passed. Caching: measured improvement in job setup time from ~45s to ~18s for node/python jobs on subsequent runs.
release_notes: Refactor CI: split monolithic CI into separate lint/test/release workflows; improve cache key hygiene and parallelism; reduce CI walltime and increase cache hit rate. No user-facing changes.
notes: Observed reduction in median CI job time and improved cache hits during pilot. Monitor for any undiscovered flaky tests introduced by parallelism. Kept legacy ci.legacy.yml for one-week fallback.
